title: kb_mcp.bash_denied reads a settings file whose permissions.deny is not a list as holding no deny rule
goal: bash_denied treats a permissions.deny value that is not a list (a string, an object, false, 0, null) as a settings file that cannot be read, so it denies every call; a missing deny key and an empty list still hold no deny rule

run:
import sys, os, json, tempfile
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import kbcommon, kb_mcp
def denied(v, key=True):
    T = tempfile.mkdtemp()
    os.makedirs(os.path.join(T, ".claude"))
    perm = {"deny": v} if key else {}
    json.dump({"permissions": perm}, open(os.path.join(T, ".claude", "settings.local.json"), "w"))
    kbcommon.HOME = type(kbcommon.HOME)(T)
    return kb_mcp.bash_denied("rm -rf x")
bad = [repr(v) for v in ("Bash", {}, False, 0, None) if denied(v) is None]
wrong = [n for n, got in [("missing key", denied(None, False)), ("empty list", denied([]))] if got is not None]
print("not-a-list read as no rule:", bad, "wrongly denied:", wrong)
sys.exit(1 if bad or wrong else 0)

clauses.clause: bash_denied treats a permissions.deny value that is not a list (a string, an object, false, 0, null) as a settings file that cannot be read, so it denies every call
a missing deny key and an empty list still hold no deny rule

notes: Found while fixing BG-syhgfwdr: bash_denied ends with 'for rule in rules if isinstance(rules, list) else []', so a permissions.deny that is a string, an object, false, 0 or null holds no deny rule instead of denying as an unreadable file does. Planned in SP-jopt2c3z (2026-10-24 day run). Premise run on base: the repro exits 1 (a deny that is a string, object, false, 0 or null reads as no rule; the missing-key and empty-list cases already hold no rule). Fix sits at the tail of bash_denied: read the deny value with a missing key as [] and any other non-list as the unreadable-file denial. No test file covers bash_denied today; the check is the planted repro (tests only for critical components, kb/_self/code.md).
